subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must combine or divide rational quantities while keeping the quantity each number names
use when a quotient is computed but its meaning as a per-unit or share size is not recoverable
anchor: A fraction names a division: a/b is the size of one part when a is shared into b equal parts, so the operation and the quantity it measures must stay attached.
ordinary_language_bridge: Say what one part is worth before writing the fraction bar, then check that the written quotient measures that same thing.
reconstruction_route: name the quantity being divided and the number of equal parts
write the division as a single fraction rather than a decimal guess
make denominators comparable before adding or subtracting
combine numerators only after denominators agree
simplify by a common factor, not by cancelling across an addition
restate the simplified value as a quantity with its unit

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: the same two rational quantities and the same operation symbol
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: combining numerators over a common denominator versus adding numerators and denominators separately
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Which result can still be read as a size of one part?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: only a common denominator makes the numerators count the same-sized parts

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: a fraction is a pair of independent numbers that may be operated on component-wise
misconception_discriminator.probe: ask the learner to state the size of one part before and after the operation
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner refuses component-wise addition and rewrites with a common denominator

repair_route: return to a part-whole statement of each fraction
rebuild a common denominator from the part sizes
recompute the combination and read the result back as a quantity
retry on a quotient that arises inside a slope or rate computation
verification_method: recompute the quotient by an independent route such as scaling both parts
check that the simplified value still answers the original per-unit question
known_limitations: does not cover irrational or surd arithmetic
does not by itself establish that a modelled ratio is constant
